title: Interpret Robotics Module Role and Geek+ AGV Command Types During Tote Task Execution
summary: Use the Robotics module description to explain how tote tasks flow from the Sorter Sweeper module to the Robotics module and then to Geek+ for AGV execution. Recognize the Robotics module’s documented Geek+ command types used during tote task execution.
when_to_use: When L1 support needs to interpret what the Robotics module is responsible for during tote task execution (state-machine role, handoff from Sorter Sweeper, and the set of Geek+ AGV command types) to guide troubleshooting discussions.
not_for: Do not use this procedure as a substitute for deeper diagnostics when live system behavior cannot be reconciled with the documented handoff (Sorter Sweeper → Robotics → Geek+).
roles_and_responsibilities: L1_support: Use the documented Robotics module responsibilities and the listed Geek+ command types to frame expected AGV actions during tote task execution and troubleshooting discussions.
access_or_tools_needed: Training video slide frame evidence from the provided video segment (Robotics module detailed design slide and command list).

visual_references.description: Sorter Sweeper module orchestration / task flow context frame describing tote task orchestration and the Robotics module handoff (Sorter Sweeper → Robotics) and related module communication context.

Robotics Module Detailed Design slide frame showing: Robotics module acts as the state machine for AGVs; receives tote tasks from Sorter Sweeper; generates commands for Geek+; includes the AGV command list (Induct tote, Remove tote, Empty go to, Pickup tote, Move tote, Drop off tote, Cancel Request, Go Charge).

steps.title: Recall the Robotics module responsibility as the AGV state machine
steps.purpose: Establish the documented ownership of AGV state-machine behavior so troubleshooting discussions correctly attribute expected AGV actions to the Robotics module.
steps.instruction: In your troubleshooting discussion, treat the Robotics module as the AGV state machine and use that framing when interpreting tote task execution behavior.
steps.expected_result: You can accurately state that the Robotics module “acts as the state machine for AGVs.”
steps.healthy_condition: Your explanation of tote task execution attributes AGV state-machine behavior to the Robotics module (not to Sorter Sweeper or Geek+ directly).
steps.failure_condition: You attribute AGV state-machine behavior to the wrong component (e.g., describing Sorter Sweeper as the AGV state machine or treating Geek+ as the state machine).

actions.label: Use the Robotics module state-machine statement
actions.exact_action: Use the documented statement: “The Robotics module acts as the state machine for AGVs.”

steps.title: Confirm the handoff: Robotics receives tote tasks from Sorter Sweeper
steps.purpose: Ensure the expected task flow is correct so you can map tote task stages to the Robotics module’s command generation.
steps.instruction: In your troubleshooting discussion, describe the handoff as: Sorter Sweeper provides tote tasks to the Robotics module, and the Robotics module then generates commands for Geek+ to execute.
steps.expected_result: You can accurately state that the Robotics module “receives tote tasks from the Sorter Sweeper module.”
steps.healthy_condition: Your task-flow explanation includes the handoff direction Sorter Sweeper → Robotics (tote tasks originate with Sorter Sweeper).
steps.failure_condition: Your task-flow explanation reverses the direction (Robotics providing tote tasks to Sorter Sweeper) or omits the handoff.

actions.label: Use the documented handoff statement
actions.exact_action: Use the documented statement: “It receives tote tasks from the Sorter Sweeper module.”

steps.title: Identify the documented Geek+ AGV command types generated by Robotics
steps.purpose: Provide the exact command vocabulary used by the Robotics module so L1 support can map tote-task stages to expected Geek+ command types during troubleshooting discussions.
steps.instruction: Use the Robotics module command list as the canonical set of Geek+ AGV command types for tote execution discussions.
steps.expected_result: You can list the documented command types: Induct tote, Remove tote, Empty go to, Pickup tote, Move tote, Drop off tote, Cancel Request, Go Charge.
steps.healthy_condition: Your list matches the documented command names and you can reference them when discussing which stage of tote execution is expected.
steps.failure_condition: You use incorrect or non-documented command names, or you omit one of the documented command types.

actions.label: Use the Robotics AGV command list
actions.exact_action: Use the documented AGV commands list: “Induct tote”, “Remove tote”, “Empty go to”, “Pickup tote”, “Move tote”, “Drop off tote”, “Cancel Request”, “Go Charge”.

steps.title: Map tote-task execution stages to the expected Robotics→Geek+ command types during troubleshooting discussions
steps.purpose: Translate a tote-task stage (induct/remove/empty/pickup/move/drop/cancel/charge) into the expected Geek+ command type vocabulary so the discussion stays consistent with the documented Robotics module behavior.
steps.instruction: When discussing a tote-task execution issue, use the documented command list to state what the Robotics module would be expected to request from Geek+ for the relevant task stage (induct/remove/empty/pickup/move/drop/cancel/charge).
steps.expected_result: You can connect the tote-task stage to the corresponding documented command type from the Robotics module list.
steps.healthy_condition: Your troubleshooting discussion uses the documented command vocabulary and aligns the stage being discussed with one of: Induct tote, Remove tote, Empty go to, Pickup tote, Move tote, Drop off tote, Cancel Request, Go Charge.
steps.failure_condition: You cannot map the stage to any documented command type, or the live behavior you observe cannot be reconciled with the documented handoff and command vocabulary.

actions.label: State expected command type for the stage
actions.exact_action: Use the documented command list to map the task stage to the expected Geek+ command type (Induct tote / Remove tote / Empty go to / Pickup tote / Move tote / Drop off tote / Cancel Request / Go Charge).

stop_or_escalate_if: If the live system behavior cannot be reconciled with the documented command types or the expected handoff (Sorter Sweeper → Robotics → Geek+), escalate to deeper system diagnostics beyond this training-derived interpretation.

success_criteria: Support can accurately describe that the Robotics module acts as the AGV state machine.
Support can accurately describe that the Robotics module receives tote tasks from the Sorter Sweeper module.
Support can name the documented Geek+ AGV command types used for tote execution: Induct tote, Remove tote, Empty go to, Pickup tote, Move tote, Drop off tote, Cancel Request, Go Charge.
During troubleshooting discussions, support can map a tote-task stage to the expected command type vocabulary.
healthy_conditions: Troubleshooting explanations consistently attribute AGV state-machine behavior to the Robotics module.
Task-flow explanations consistently include Sorter Sweeper → Robotics → Geek+.
Command vocabulary used in discussions matches the documented list.
failure_conditions: AGV state-machine responsibility is attributed to the wrong component.
Task-flow direction is incorrect or missing (Sorter Sweeper → Robotics → Geek+).
Command names used in discussion do not match the documented Robotics module command list.
Live behavior cannot be reconciled with the documented handoff/command vocabulary.
escalation_guidance: Escalate to deeper system diagnostics beyond this training-derived interpretation if live system behavior cannot be reconciled with the documented command types or the expected handoff (Sorter Sweeper → Robotics → Geek+).
